Problem a

Assume that there is no price or limitation on CO2 emissions in the Landic electricity market. Calculate the electricity price and the total CO2 emissions per year.

We are looking for

  • Electricty price
  • CO2 emissions
We assume a price range of (300, 450), and solve: ||[ \frac{ \lambda - \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C }{\beta_{\text{coal, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C} G_{\text{coal, max}}+ \frac{ \lambda - \beta_{\text{bio, min}}^C }{\beta_{\text{bio, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{bio, min}}^C} G_{\text{bio, max}}= 11, ||]
which gives us ||[\lambda = 370.0 \text{ ¤/MWh} \\ \text{CO2 emissions} = 7000.0 \text{ kton/MWh} = 7.0 \text{ Mton/MWh} ||]

Problem b

Assume that Land introduced a tax of 45 ¤/ton for CO2 emissions. Calculate the electricity price and the total CO2 emissions per year.

Data

  • CO2 tax = 45 ¤/ton ||(\Rightarrow||) 0.045 ¤/kg

We are looking for

  • Electricity price
  • CO2 emissions
We assume a price range in (300, 450) and solve ||[ \frac{ \lambda - (\beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C + \beta^E_\text{coal} \tau) }{\beta_{\text{coal, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C} G_{\text{coal, max}}+ \frac{ \lambda - \beta_{\text{bio, min}}^C }{\beta_{\text{bio, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{bio, min}}^C} G_{\text{bio, max}}= 11, ||]
which gives us ||[\lambda = 385.0 \text{ ¤/MWh} \\ \text{CO2 emissions} = 4000.0 \text{ kton/MWh} = 4.0 \text{ Mton/MWh} ||]

Problem c

Assume that a feebate system is introduced in the Landic electricity market. The feebate system requires producers to pay a fee per ton CO2 emissions and then the sum of all CO2 fees is paid back to the involved power plants proportional to their share of the generation. How large must the CO2 fee be in order to result in any reduction of the CO2 emissions?

Unkowns

  • price
  • payback
  • CO2 emissions fee

Constraints

  • less CO2

Solve for CO2 emissions fee

||[ \beta_{\text{gas, min}}^C + \beta_{\text{gas}}^E \varphi - \rho \leq \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C + \beta_{\text{coal}}^E \varphi - \rho \Rightarrow ||]||[ \beta_{\text{gas, min}}^C + \beta_{\text{gas}}^E \varphi \leq \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C + \beta_{\text{coal}}^E \varphi \Rightarrow ||]||[ \varphi \leq \frac{\beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C - \beta_{\text{gas, min}}^C}{\beta_{\text{gas}}^E - \beta_{\text{coal}}^E} = 0.3 \text{ ¤/kg} ||]

We assume a price range of (300, 600) and get the following equations ||[ \frac{ \lambda - (\beta_{\text{gas, min}}^C + \beta_{\text{gas}}^E \varphi - \rho)}{\beta_{\text{gas, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{gas, min}}^C} G_{\text{gas, max}} + \frac{ \lambda - (\beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C + \beta_{\text{coal}}^E \varphi - \rho)}{\beta_{\text{coal, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C} G_{\text{coal, max}}+\\ \frac{ \lambda - \beta_{\text{bio, min}}^C }{\beta_{\text{bio, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{bio, min}}^C} G_{\text{bio, max}}= 11, ||]||[ \varphi \big (\beta_{\text{gas}}^E \frac{ \lambda - (\beta_{\text{gas, min}}^C + \beta_{\text{gas}}^E \varphi - \rho)}{\beta_{\text{gas, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{gas, min}}^C} G_{\text{gas, max}}+ \beta_{\text{coal}}^E \frac{ \lambda - (\beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C + \beta_{\text{coal}}^E \varphi - \rho)}{\beta_{\text{coal, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C}G_{\text{coal, max}} \big) \\ = \rho \big (\frac{ \lambda - (\beta_{\text{gas, min}}^C + \beta_{\text{gas}}^E \varphi - \rho)}{\beta_{\text{gas, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{gas, min}}^C} G_{\text{gas, max}}+ \frac{ \lambda - (\beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C + \beta_{\text{coal}}^E \varphi - \rho)}{\beta_{\text{coal, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C} G_{\text{coal, max}}\big), ||]

By solving the equations we get two candidates: Solution 1: ||[ \lambda_1 = 390.0 \text{ ¤/MWh}\\ \rho_1 = 225.0 \text{ ¤/MWh}\\ \varphi = 0.3\text{ ¤/kg} \\ \text{CO2 emissions} = 2250 \text{ kton/MWh} ||]Solution 2: ||[ \lambda_2 = 405.0 \text{ ¤/MWh} \\ \rho_2 = 195.0 \text{ ¤/MWh}\\ \varphi = 0.3\text{ ¤/kg} \\ \text{CO2 emissions} = 0 \text{ kton/MWh} ||]

Problem d

Assume that tradable green certificates are introduces in the Landic electricity market. Green certificates are issued for electricity generation from solar PV, wind power and biofuels. The penalty fee for missing certificates is 1 000 ¤/MWh. How high must the quota for green certificates be in order to reduce the emissions to 5 Mton/year? What will the electricity price and price of green certificates become with this quota

Data

  • Penalty fee = 1000 EUR/MWh
  • Total emissions = 5 Mton / year
  • Participating sources = Solar PV, wind power and biofuels

We are looking for

  • Quota for green certificates
  • Electricity price
  • Green certificate price

Assume price between (300, 450) EUR/MWh ||[ G_{\text{solar, max}} + G_{\text{wind, max}} + G_{\text{hydro, max}} + G_{\text{nuclear, max}} + G_{\text{bio}} + G_{\text{coal}} + G_{\text{gas}} = 420 ||]||[ G_{\text{solar, max}} + G_{\text{wind, max}} + G_{\text{bio}} = 420x, ||]||[ \beta_{\text{coal}}^E \frac{ \lambda - \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C}{\beta_{\text{coal, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^c} G_{\text{coal, max}} = 5000 ||]where ||(x||) green certificate quota.
Solving the equations gives us ||[ x = 0.2619 = 26.19 \% \\ \lambda = 350.0 \text{ ¤/MWh}\\ \text{Certificate price} = 30.0 \text{ ¤/MWh} ||]

Problem e

Assume that electricity disclosure is introduced in the Landic electricity market. The demand for renewable electricity (i.e., solar, wind, hydro and biofuels) is 333 TWh/year and these consumers are willing to pay up to 100 ¤/MWh extra for renewable electricity (compared to the price of grey electricity). Calculate the electricity price for renewable electricity and grey electricity respectively as well as the total CO2 emissions per year.

Data

  • Renewable demand = 333 TWh/year
  • ||(\Delta||)Premium = 100 EUR/MWh

We are looking for

  • Renewable electricity price
  • Grey electricity price
  • Total CO2 emissions per year

Let ||(\lambda_g||) be the grey electricity price, assume a price range of (300, 400) => Demand = 420 - 333 - 83 =4 TWh/year ||[ \frac{ \lambda_g - \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C }{\beta_{\text{coal, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C} G_{\text{coal, max}} = 4 \text{ TWh/year}, ||]solving this gives us ||[ \lambda_g = 340\text{{ ¤/MWh}}. ||]

Let ||(\lambda_r||) be the renewable electricity price, assume a price range of (350, ||(\lambda_g + 100 = 440||)) => Demand = 333 - 326 = 7 TWh/year ||[ \frac{ \lambda_r - \beta_{\text{bio, min}}^C }{\beta_{\text{bio, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{bio, min}}^C} G_{\text{bio, max}} = 7\text{ TWh/year} ||]solving this gives us ||[ \lambda_r = 385.\text{{ ¤/MWh}} ||]And finally the total emisssions per year in this case are ||[ \text{CO2 emissions} = 4 \text{ Mton/year} ||]

Problem f

Assume that tradable emission rights are introduced in the Landic electricity market. The penalty fee for emitting 1 ton CO2 without holding an emission right is set to 1 000 ¤/ton. The number of emission rights is set to 3.5 Mton/year. Calculate the electricity price and the price of emission rights.

Data

  • Penalty fee = 1000 ¤/ton
  • Number of emission rights = 3.5 Mton/year

We are looking for

  • Electricity price
  • Price of the emission rights

Assume that the emissions are equal to the cap ||(\Rightarrow \xi < 1000||), further assume a price range of (300, 450). ||[ \frac{ \lambda - (\beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C + \xi )}{\beta_{\text{coal, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C} G_{\text{coal, max}}+ \frac{ \lambda - \beta_{\text{bio, min}}^C }{\beta_{\text{bio, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{bio, min}}^C} G_{\text{bio, max}}= 11 ||]||[ \beta_{\text{coal}}^E \frac{ \lambda - (\beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C + \xi )}{\beta_{\text{coal, max}}^C - \beta_{\text{coal, min}}^C}G_{\text{coal, max}} = 3500 ||]
Solving the equations gives us ||[ \lambda = 387.5 \text{ ¤/MWh} \\ \xi = 52.5 \text{ ¤/MWh}.\\ ||]

Problem h

In this question you will need to use the excel workbook Nordic price to analyse the Nordic electricity market. The model itself is found on the first sheet (“Overview”). Additional data, sources and calculations are found on the other two sheets. For this problem, you will however only need to edit the blue fields in the overview. The model will use the simple price model explained in the lectures on electricity pricing for a rough estimate of the Nordic electricity price. The default data in the model is for 2019, which was a fairly average year in terms of hydro inflow. Which electricity prices would be obtained if 2019 had been a wet year (75 TWh hydro power in Swe- den, 140 TWh in Norway and 16 TWh in Finland) or a dry year (55 TWh hydro power in Sweden, 110 TWh in Norway and 12 TWh in Finland). Compare the impact of hydro inflow on electricity prices to the impact if the fifth Finnish nuclear power plant Olkiluoto 3 had been operational in 2019? The annual generation from Olkiluoto 3 is expected to be between 12 and 13 TWh/year.
